newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: State authority clears Crown casino licence.
newsitem.headline: State authority clears Crown casino licence.

text.p: The Victoria state government said on Monday the state's casino authority had cleared Crown Ltd to continue to operate the state's only casino licence.

"The Victorian Casino and Gaming Authority (VCGA) formed a unanimous opinion that during the period under review, the casino operator was suitable to continue to hold the licence and it was in the public interest that the casino licence should remain in force," the government said in a statement.
Under the state's Casino Control Act, the VCGA has to investigate and report within three years of the casino's start-up whether the operator is suitable to continue to hold the licence.
Crown's major shareholder, Hudson Conway Ltd, is the subject of a long running police inquiry into a collapsed property deal.
Victoria's Finance and Gaming Minister Roger Hallam said the VCGA's report did not include three independent inquiries into issues under investigation by other bodies or before the courts.
"The VCGA received legal advice that it would be inappropriate and disruptive to initiate a separate inquiry," Hallam said.
The suitability of the casino operator was constantly under review by the VCGA which could take action at any time, he said.
